questions.text:
A non-pipelined CPU has 12 general purpose registers?(R0,R1,R2,...,R12). Following operations are supported

ADD Ra, Rb, Rr Add Ra to Rb and store the result in Rr
MUL Ra, Rb, Rr Multiply Ra to Rb and store the result in Rr

MUL operation takes two clock cycles, ADD takes one clock cycle.

Calculate minimum number of clock cycles required to compute the value of the expression XY+XYZ+YZ. The variable X,Y,Z are initially available in registers R0,R1 and R2 and contents of these registers must not be modified.
questions.solution:
Factor to save multiplications: [latex]XY+XYZ+YZ=Y(XZ+X+Z)[/latex].
1. MUL R0, R2, R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] XZ (2 cycles)
2. ADD R0, R2, R4 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] X + Z (1 cycle)
3. ADD R3, R4, R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] XZ + X + Z (1 cycle)
4. MUL R3, R1, R3 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] Y(XZ + X + Z) (2 cycles)

Total = 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 6 cycles (two multiplications are unavoidable).

Answer: 6

questions.text:
An array of 2 two byte integers is stored in big endian machine in byte addresses as shown below. What will be its storage pattern in little endian machine ?
[latex]\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Address}& \text{Data}\\\hline0 \times 104&78\\0 \times 103&56\\0 \times 102&34\\0 \times 101&12\end{array}[/latex]
questions.solution:
In big endian the most significant byte is at the lower address, so the two integers are 0x1234 (at 0x101-0x102) and 0x5678 (at 0x103-0x104).

Little endian stores the least significant byte first:
- 0x101: 34, 0x102: 12
- 0x103: 78, 0x104: 56

Answer: 0x104: 56, 0x103: 78, 0x102: 12, 0x101: 34

questions.text:
Which of the following affects the processing power assuming they do not influence each other
1. Data bus capability
2. Address scheme
3. Clock speed
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Data bus width: more bits moved per transfer.
- Addressing scheme: affects how fast operands can be reached and how much memory is usable.
- Clock speed: more operations per second.

All three affect processing power.

Answer: 1, 2 and 3

questions.text: Statements associated with registers of a CPU are given. Identify the false statement.
questions.solution:
The program counter holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched, not the one being executed. The other statements describe normal fetch/decode behaviour.

Answer: The program counter holds the memory address of the instruction in execution (FALSE)

questions.text:
The immediate addressing mode can be used for
1. Loading internal registers with initial values
2. Perform arithmetic or logical operation on data contained in instructions
Which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
In immediate mode the operand value is part of the instruction itself, e.g. MOV R1, #5 or ADD R1, #3.
- It can load registers with initial (constant) values.
- It can do arithmetic/logic with that constant.

Both uses are valid; it has nothing to do with the cache.

Answer: Both 1 and 2
